conclusion: numpy scalar np.interp on float64 grids computes fma(x - x0, (y1 - y0) / (x1 - x0), y0): slope-first, then a single-rounding fused multiply-add (compiler fp-contraction; build-dependent). All unfused algebraic equivalents differ by 1 ulp on 9-36% of interior points. Consequence: no pure-Python transcription on runtimes without fast fma (this env: Python 3.11, no math.fma) can be both bit-exact and faster than the current dispatch.

corpus.endpoints: 0.0 and 1.0 exact; below-range and above-range values

corpus.knots: every knot exactly, plus nextafter(knot,-inf) and nextafter(knot,+inf)
corpus.result: fused-slope form 60000/60000 exact; F1 9.2% mismatch; F2 11.6%; F3/F4/F6 30-36%; F8/F9 13-14%
